paraphrase: Objection: action is enjoined by the Veda as knowledge is; it is a duty and assists knowledge; scripture declares a fault in omitting it; as a sacrifice needs its accessories, knowledge needs prescribed acts. Reply: knowledge, the final mental mode lit by pure awareness, destroys the whole apparatus of agent, act and instrument on which action depends; so the wise should give up action entirely — knowledge and action cannot be combined, being opposed — and remain devoted to contemplating the Self.

paraphrase: Having negated all by 'not this' and tasted the nectar of consciousness in the heart, give up the world as one gives up the fruit's rind after drinking its juice. The Self is never born, never dies, neither wanes nor grows. Superimposition (adhyāsa) is imagining one thing in another, as a snake in a rope; ego is the first superimposition on the Self; the jīva is consciousness reflected in the intellect born of beginningless ignorance, while the Self stands apart as the intellect's witness; by their mutual superimposition, like fire and iron in a heated ball, the insentient seems conscious and the conscious insentient.
